title: is_valid_fetch_host allows @ in hostname, enabling userinfo injection
description: A mailbox_host value like 'attacker@peer.ts.net' passes is_valid_fetch_host because ends_with('.ts.net') matches without stripping userinfo first. The URL becomes https://attacker@peer.ts.net/... which most HTTP clients interpret as userinfo, not as a hostname prefix. In practice today mailbox_host comes from WhoIs node_name (Tailscale-controlled, no @ allowed), so this is not immediately exploitable. But the guard does not enforce its own stated contract: it is supposed to validate the host portion only. Any future code path that stores or supplies a mailbox_host from a less-vetted source (e.g. a Contact/set owner call, a migration, or a test fixture) would bypass the SSRF check silently. Fix: add an explicit early return false if the ip_part (or the raw host before port stripping) contains '@'.
